formal_statement: ∀ (a b c : ℕ), 2 * a < b → ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n → ¬ ∃ (q : ℕ) (w : (Fin n → Bool) → List Bool), 0 < q ∧ q ^ b ≤ n ^ a ∧ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.QueryLocal n q w ∧ (∀ x : Fin n → Bool, (w x).length ≤ n ^ c + c) ∧ (∀ x : Fin n → Bool, (Finset.univ.filter fun i : Fin n => x i = true).card % 2 = 1 ↔ w x ∈ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.PartialMCSP) ∧ ∀ (n' s : ℕ) (T : List (Option Bool)), w (fun _ : Fin n => false) = List.replicate s true ++ false :: PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.encodePartial T → T.length = 2 ^ n' → ∃ f : (Fin n' → Bool) → Bool, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Consistent n' T f ∧ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.HasCircuitSize n' f (q * (Nat.log 2 n + 1) ^ c)
plain_statement: CONJECTURE, a corollary of L-meta-030, not found stated in print: for an exponent a/b < 1/2 and a constant c, at every large enough n there is no map from n-bit inputs to strings of length at most n^c + c that reduces parity to partial MCSP, is q-local with q >= 1 and q^b <= n^a, and whose partial table on the all-false input has a consistent circuit of size q (log2 n + 1)^c. Reductions computable in local time q meet the last hypothesis by zero completion (L-meta-017), outside this statement. Extends the 2017 local reduction theorem for MCSP to partial MCSP.
title: TARGET: no q-local reduction of parity to partial MCSP for q below n^(a/b), a/b < 1/2, with a simple zero-input table
